name: Familial Partial Lipodystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Partial Lipodystrophy

criteria.description: Progressive loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue in the limbs and trunk with relative fat accumulation in face and neck
Presence of insulin resistance, diabetes mellitus, or dyslipidemia
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes such as LMNA, PPARG, or AKT2
Clinical evidence of muscular hypertrophy in affected regions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of regional adipose tissue loss plus metabolic complications, with or without genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not always necessary if clinical features are typical.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Regional loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue in limbs and trunk
searchTerms: localized fat loss in arms and trunk
patchy loss of fat under skin on limbs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Relative fat accumulation in face and neck
searchTerms: increased fat around face and neck
fat accumulation in facial and neck areas
relative facial and neck fat buildup
high triglycerides and low good cholesterol
female hormone disorder with cystic ovaries
mood disorders including sadness and worry

laboratory: Elevated fasting insulin and glucose levels indicating insulin resistance
Elevated liver enzymes consistent with hepatic steatosis
imaging: MRI or CT showing selective loss of subcutaneous fat in limbs and trunk
Ultrasound or MRI evidence of fatty liver
genetic: Pathogenic variants in LMNA gene (most common)
Variants in PPARG, AKT2, or other related genes

distinguishingFeatures: Complete or near-complete absence of adipose tissue rather than regional loss
Earlier onset in infancy or childhood
Onset typically in childhood or adolescence without family history
Loss of fat predominantly in face and upper body

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe insulin resistance with regional fat loss
Family history of similar fat distribution abnormalities
Early development of diabetes and dyslipidemia in young adults
references: Garg A. Lipodystrophies. Am J Med. 2000;108(2):143-152.
Agarwal AK, Garg A. Genetic disorders of adipose tissue development, differentiation, and death. Annu Rev Genomics Hum Genet. 2006;7:175-199.
Brown RJ, Araujo-Vilar D, Cheung PT, et al. The diagnosis and management of lipodystrophy syndromes: A multi-society practice guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2016;101(12):4500-4511.
